title: RBI Issues Final Rules on Money Mule Accounts for Banks
description: RBI finalizes amendment directions requiring banks to implement SOP for temporary debit holds on suspected money mule accounts, effective July 2027.
quick: The Reserve Bank of India has issued final amendment directions on suspected money mule accounts to prevent cyber-enabled financial frauds. The directions establish a standard operating procedure for banks to place temporary debit holds on suspicious accounts and coordinate with law enforcement, while protecting genuine…
points: Final directions issued after stakeholder feedback on September draft
SOP mandates temporary debit holds on suspected money mule accounts
Banks must coordinate with law enforcement agencies to remove holds
Effective July 1, 2027, or earlier at bank's discretion
Applies to commercial, small finance, payments, rural, and cooperative banks
body: The Reserve Bank of India has issued final amendment directions on suspected money mule accounts aimed at preventing cyber-enabled financial frauds. The directions follow a draft released on September 11, 2026, which received stakeholder feedback that has been incorporated into the final version.

The directions establish a standard operating procedure requiring banks to place temporary debit holds on accounts or amounts suspected to be linked to money mule activity. Banks must coordinate with law enforcement agencies to remove such holds while ensuring genuine customers are not inconvenienced.

The amendment directions apply to commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks, and urban co-operative banks. They take effect from July 1, 2027, though banks may implement the SOP earlier at their discretion.

faq.q: When do the new RBI money mule account rules take effect?
faq.a: The directions take effect from July 1, 2027, or from an earlier date if a bank decides to implement the standard operating procedure sooner.

faq.q: Which types of banks must follow these amendment directions?
faq.a: The directions apply to commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks, and urban co-operative banks.
